Le Bon Marché. The first modern department store. Paris. 1875.

Le Bon Marché (the good market" in French) is a department store in Paris. Founded in 1852 by Aristide Boucicaut, it was the first ever modern department store.

Originally a novelty shop, in 1852, the owners instituted fixed prices, guarantees that allowed exchanges and refunds, extensive newspaper advertising, and a much wider variety of merchandise. They also installed a reading room for husbands while their wives shopped; entertainment for children, and sent out six million catalogs. By 1880 half the employees were women; unmarried women employees lived in dormitories on the upper floors. The annual income of the store increased from 500,000 francs in 1852 to five million in 1860.
